title: Dasakam 13 — Hiranyākṣa Vadha
description: Nārāyaṇa as Varāha defeats Hiraṇyākṣa, is praised as the embodiment of yajña, and returns to Vaikuṇṭha.

stanzas.sanskrit:
हिरण्याक्षं तावद्वरद भवदन्वेषणपरं
चरन्तं सांवर्ते पयसि निजजङ्घापरिमिते ।
भवद्भक्तो गत्वा कपटपटुधीर्नारदमुनिः
शनैरूचे नन्दन् दनुजमपि निन्दंस्तव बलम् ॥ १३-१ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
hiraṇyākṣaṃ tāvadvarada bhavadanveṣaṇaparaṃ
carantaṃ sāṃvarte payasi nijajaṅghāparimite |
bhavadbhakto gatvā kapaṭapaṭudhīrnāradamuniḥ
śanairūce nandan danujamapi nindaṃstava balam || 13-1 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Sage Naradha who is skillfully diplomatic in furthering Bhagwan’s avatara purposes, approached Hiranyaksha, who was running about searching for Bhagwan in the cosmic waters which barely reached his knees. Naradha calmly spoke to him, praising him and undermining Bhagwan’s prowess.

stanzas.sanskrit:
स मायावी विष्णुर्हरति भवदीयां वसुमतीं
प्रभो कष्टं कष्टं किमिदमिति तेनाभिगदितः ।
नदन् क्वासौ क्वासाविति स मुनिना दर्शितपथो
भवन्तं सम्प्रापद्धरणिधरमुद्यन्तमुदकात् ॥ १३-२ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
sa māyāvī viṣṇurharati bhavadīyāṃ vasumatīṃ
prabho kaṣṭaṃ kaṣṭaṃ kimidamiti tenābhigaditaḥ |
nadan kvāsau kvāsāviti sa muninā darśitapatho
bhavantaṃ samprāpaddharaṇidharamudyantamudakāt || 13-2 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Naradha told that decietful  Vishnu was stealing away HIS own earth. Hiranyaksha fierce with anger roared big going in search and spotted  Bhagwan rising up the waters with the earth.

stanzas.sanskrit:
अहो आरण्योऽयं मृग इति हसन्तं बहुतरै-
-दुरुक्तैर्विध्यन्तं दितिसुतमवज्ञाय भगवन् ।
महीं दृष्ट्वा दंष्ट्राशिरसि चकितां स्वेन महसा
पयोधावाधाय प्रसभमुदयुङ्क्था मृधविधौ ॥ १३-३ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
aho āraṇyo’yaṃ mṛga iti hasantaṃ bahutarai-
-rduruktairvidhyantaṃ ditisutamavajñāya bhagavan |
mahīṃ dṛṣṭvā daṃṣṭrāśirasi cakitāṃ svena mahasā
payodhāvādhāya prasabhamudayuṅkthā mṛdhavidhau || 13-3 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Hurling abuses at the Lord Varaha for its look of a wild boar, Hiranyaksha got ready to fight. Bhagwan lowered down the trembling Goddess Earth carefully from his tusk on to the sea floor and got ready to fight back.

stanzas.sanskrit:
गदापाणौ दैत्ये त्वमपि हि गृहीतोन्नतगदो
नियुद्धेन क्रीडन् घटघटरवोद्घुष्टवियता ।
रणालोकौत्सुक्यान्मिलति सुरसङ्घे द्रुतममुं
निरुन्ध्याः सन्ध्यातः प्रथममिति धात्रा जगदिषे ॥ १३-४ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
gadāpāṇau daitye tvamapi hi gṛhītonnatagado
niyuddhena krīḍan ghaṭaghaṭaravodghuṣṭaviyatā |
raṇālokautsukyānmilati surasaṅghe drutamamuṃ
nirundhyāḥ sandhyātaḥ prathamamiti dhātrā jagadiṣe || 13-4 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: As Hiranyaksha was armed with mace, Lord Varaha too sported a mace and was playfully fighting with him. As the maces struck with each other, with huge sound, host of Gods assembled in the sky to witness the fight. Brahma cautioned Lord Varaha to kill Hiranyaksha before night fall.

stanzas.sanskrit:
गदोन्मर्दे तस्मिंस्तव खलु गदायां दितिभुवो
गदाघाताद्भूमौ झटिति पतितायामहह भोः ।
मृदुस्मेरास्यस्त्वं दनुजकुलनिर्मूलनचणं
महाचक्रं स्मृत्वा करभुवि दधानो रुरुचिषे ॥ १३-५ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
gadonmarde tasmiṃstava khalu gadāyāṃ ditibhuvo
gadāghātādbhūmau jhaṭiti patitāyāmaha bhoḥ |
mṛdusmerāsyastvaṃ danujakulanirmūlanacaṇaṃ
mahācakraṃ smṛtvā karabhuvi dadhāno ruruciṣe || 13-5 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: During the fight, Hiranyaksha knocked down Lord Varaha’s mace. Smiling at this action, Bhagwan invoked the Sudarshan Chakra which is well known for slaying of the race of the Asuras. Bhagwan looked magnificent as the invoked discus placed itself in HIS hands.

stanzas.sanskrit:
ततः शूलं कालप्रतिमरुषि दैत्ये विसृजति
त्वयि छिन्दत्येनत् करकलितचक्रप्रहरणात् ।
समारुष्टो मुष्ट्या स खलु वितुदंस्त्वां समतनोत्
गलन्माये मायास्त्वयि किल जगन्मोहनकरीः ॥ १३-६ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tataḥ śūlaṃ kālapratimaruṣi daitye visṛjati
tvayi chindatyenat karakalitacakrapraharaṇāt |
samāruṣṭo muṣṭyā sa khalu vitudaṃstvāṃ samatanot
galanmāye māyāstvayi kila jaganmohanakarīḥ || 13-6 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Angered by rage, Hiranyaksha threw a trident on Lord Varaha, which was again broken down by Sudarshan chakra. Hiranyaksha hit  Lord Varaha with his fist and with Maya tried many feats of warfare only to lose all before Bhagwan, who is above all maya.

stanzas.sanskrit:
भवच्चक्रज्योतिष्कणलवनिपातेन विधुते
ततो मायाचक्रे विततघनरोषान्धमनसम् ।
गरिष्ठाभिर्मुष्टिप्रहृतिभिरभिघ्नन्तमसुरं
स्वपादाङ्गुष्ठेन श्रवणपदमूले निरवधीः ॥ १३-७ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
bhavaccakrajyotiṣkaṇalavanipātena vidhute
tato māyācakre vitataghanaroṣāndhamanasam |
gariṣṭhābhirmuṣṭiprahṛtibhirabhighnantamasuraṃ
svapādāṅguṣṭhena śravaṇapadamūle niravadhīḥ || 13-7 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: The illusions created by asura were all nullified by Lord Varaha's discus. He then resorted to heavy blows with his mighty fists when Lord Varaha, gave a deathly blow with his big toe at the base of the asura's ear.

stanzas.sanskrit:
महाकायः सोऽयं तव चरणपातप्रमथितो
गलद्रक्तो वक्त्रादपतदृषिभिः श्लाघितहतिः ।
तदा त्वामुद्दामप्रमदभरविद्योतिहृदया
मुनीन्द्राः सान्द्राभिः स्तुतिभिरनुवन्नध्वरतनुम् ॥ १३-८ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
mahākāyaḥ so’yaṃ tava caraṇapātapramathito
galadrakto vaktrādapatadṛṣibhiḥ ślāghitahatiḥ |
tadā tvāmuddāmapramadabharavidyotihṛdayā
munīndrāḥ sāndrābhiḥ stutibhiranuvannadhvaratanum || 13-8 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: That gigantic Asura crushed by the powerful blow of Lord Varaha, fell down with blood flowing out of his mouth. Sages and Gods were delighted and sang hyms in appreciation of  Varaha Murthy brimming with joy.

stanzas.sanskrit:
त्वचि छन्दो रोमस्वपि कुशगणश्चक्षुषि घृतं
चतुर्होतारोऽङ्घ्रौ स्रुगपि वदने चोदर इडा ।
ग्रहा जिह्वायां ते परपुरुष कर्णे च चमसा
विभो सोमो वीर्यं वरद गलदेशेऽप्युपसदः ॥ १३-९ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tvaci chando romasvapi kuśagaṇaścakṣuṣi ghṛtaṃ
caturhotāro’ṅghrau srugapi vadane codara iḍā |
grahā jihvāyāṃ te parapuruṣa karṇe ca camasā
vibho somo vīryaṃ varada galadeśe’pyupasadaḥ || 13-9 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Bhagwan’s skin are the Vedic Mantras, hair are the 'kusha' grass, eyes are the ghee, feet are the four sacrificing priests, face is 'sruk',( the ladle for sacrifice) and  stomach is the 'Ida' (the vessel which holds the sacrificial ingredients), tongue is the soma pot, ears are the chamasas (the vessel which holds the sacrificial remnants) and  virility is soma, neck are the sacrifices called Upasat, (the subsidiary rites) and the entire body is the embodiment of the holy Yagna.

stanzas.sanskrit:
मुनीन्द्रैरित्यादिस्तवनमुखरैर्मोदितमना
महीयस्या मूर्त्या विमलतरकीर्त्या च विलसन् ।
स्वधिष्ण्यं सम्प्राप्तः सुखरसविहारी मधुरिपो
निरुन्ध्या रोगं मे सकलमपि वातालयपते ॥ १३-१० ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
munīndrairityādistavanamukharairmoditamanā
mahīyasyā mūrtyā vimalatarakīrtyā ca vilasan |
svadhiṣṇyaṃ samprāptaḥ sukharasavihārī madhuripo
nirundhyā rogaṃ me sakalamapi vātālayapate || 13-10 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Pleased with the hyms on his countless glory, Bhagwan concluded purpose ofHIS avatar and retired to Vaikunta. Bhattathiri requested Lord Guruvayoorappan to be pleased with him, and help him overcome his ailments. Bhagwan acknowledged his request immediately by nodding  head.
